record.tranche_reason: The study tests downstream performance across model sizes and measures validation loss across architectural variants, but does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting procedure.
record.gate_note: The study does not fit power laws to held-out cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens, or compute, test extrapolation from smaller runs, or optimize parameter/token allocation at fixed compute. Its reported validation-loss ablations and its size-sweep benchmark results bear on V4 and V6. The cited results from other work are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: An architecture paper, not a scaling study. It bears on two versions incidentally, in a new setting (the Extender architecture, 199M–924M). For V6, it reports CORE and RULER scores at three Chinchilla-budget sizes (Table 8). For V4, it reports validation loss for architectural variants at roughly fixed parameter count (Tables 4–5). It fits no power laws, tests no extrapolation and runs no compute-allocation sweep. T2 overstates its aim; T3 fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that the Extender, with 32 extension features per layer, matches the Reference Transformer on short-context CORE and outperforms it on long-context RULER at 199M–924M. They also report a 104× smaller persistent attention memory at 920M/64k. Within the sizes tested, accuracy improves with size for CORE and RULER 1–2k, while beyond-training-context RULER is less predictable. Larger scales and token budgets were untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a new log-structured Transformer architecture, architectural ablations, and downstream benchmark performance across three sizes. It does not use the original studies' held-out-loss scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Architectural choices in the Extender affect validation loss and benchmark performance; the paper reports variation across query inputs, FFN inputs, extension widths, and V windows. Long-context RULER trends across model size are less predictable than CORE and short-context results.
record.problems: Only three Extender size classes are tested, and the authors say they could not test much larger models due to resource constraints. Token budgets are largely limited to 20× parameter count. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the listed loss or benchmark values. The scaling-related benchmark sweep is for Extender models, not a comparable sweep of both architectures.
record.rows_left_out: Detailed per-task RULER results and the broader architecture-comparison plots were not included: the size-scaling evidence is reported as aggregates in Table 8, and the other per-task comparisons do not report a size trend in a text/table form suitable for additional rows.

untested.parts: No power-law fits of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep. Chinchilla 20 tokens/param is assumed, not tested.
No depth-versus-width or aspect-ratio sweep at fixed parameter count. Only Extender wiring choices and Extender versus Transformer are compared, at two sizes.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer scaling. The ProLong mid-training and distillation runs are not size sweeps.
No fitted relation of downstream score to scale or loss. Only three sizes, one model per size, no uncertainty.
No comparison of exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: RULER 1k–8k and CORE scores for each Table 4 ablation variant and for the Table 5 variants vs the Transformer. These show near-equal validation loss with very different long-context scores, bearing on loss-to-downstream predictability.
Transformer size sweep 198M/436M/920M on CORE. 10 of 22 tasks were non-monotonic in size, and T-mono was selected on that basis.

record.verdict_notes: Scaling evidence is incidental: three sizes, one seed, no uncertainty, no fits. The V4 link is loose: the variants are Extender wiring choices rather than depth/width shape, and several change parameter count (concatenated Wq, dε). The Table 5 ablations use 9.6B tokens for the 920M class, half the Chinchilla budget. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute power-law fits.
No prediction of larger-run loss from fits to smaller runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling.
Does not sweep depth or width at fixed parameter count; reported architectural variants are not shown to have exactly matched parameter counts.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law tests.
Tests selected CORE and RULER benchmark scores across three Extender sizes, not general downstream-task predictability or prediction from pretraining loss.
No comparison of scaling-law exponents or fitting choices, nor a test of bending away from a power law.
